text:
tara: Heads-up: onboarding whirl9b (int4) into staging fleet. Hit a couple OOMs when customers do long-chat exports (800-1500 tokens). Anyone seen similar fragmentation / kv pressure patterns?

ben: Can you share the exact serving config and a short log snippet? quick hunch: variable-length batching + lazy eviction.

tara: Log excerpt and config: 
```
[2026-04-05T11:40:12Z] req=xx9a model=whirl9b-int4 max_new_tokens=1200 batch=4 seq_ctx=64 mem_before=11.9GB mem_after=+3.6GB
[2026-04-05T11:40:12Z] runtime: slab_frag=0.51 kv_free_slots=9
[2026-04-05T11:40:12Z] gpu0: OOM at kv_alloc, serving/allocator/slab.cc:310
[2026-04-05T11:40:12Z] fallback: prefix_evict reclaimed=32MB; retry -> slow success
```
serving.yml snippet: 
```yaml
model: whirl9b-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 5
  batch_timeout_ms: 10
  allow_variable_lengths: true
runtime:
  max_new_tokens_default: 1024
  kv_eviction: lazy
  slot_compaction: disabled
```

perf-bot: Staging snapshot: p50=130ms, p95=360ms, p99=2.0s, OOMs=2 in 1h, avg_tokens=480

hao: Fragmentation at 0.5 is high. Lazy eviction + variable-length microbatches = many small free segments. Two quick mitigations: reduce batch size and enable slot compaction. Also consider length bucketing to avoid mixing 50-token and 1200-token requests.

ben: Also try reducing max_new_tokens_default to 320 for the int4 variant; quant noise accumulates on very long gens and we've seen quality drift. Provide per-route opt-in if customer needs >320.

tara: Did a small experiment: rolled patch at 11:55 -> 
```yaml
batching:
  max_batch_size: 2
  batch_timeout_ms: 6
  length_bucketing: true
runtime:
  max_new_tokens_default: 320
  kv_eviction: eager
  slot_compaction: enabled
  slab_soft_reserve: 384MB
```
Rolled to staging pool at 11:58.

ops-bot: Deploy complete: whirl9b-int4 v2026-04-05T11:58 by tara -> staging-pool-3

perf-bot: Update @12:20: p99 dropped to 1.05s, OOMs=0 in 30m, slab_frag=0.33, mem_headroom +1.3GB

h: Looks promising. tara, can you run a quick quality sanity check on long-form summarization? want to ensure user-facing regressions are acceptable.

tara: Ran 300-sample check (mix of 200-1400 target tokens). Results: int4 rougeL delta vs fp16 = -1.5 pts (previously -2.9). p95 latency up ~4% due to compaction overhead. Overall acceptable.

ben: Great. Next steps proposal:
- Set whirl9b-int4 defaults: max_new_tokens_default=320, max_batch_size=2, length_bucketing=true, slot_compaction=enabled, slab_soft_reserve=384MB, kv_eviction=eager.
- Implement batcher change to prefer grouping by max_new_tokens bucket: bins [0-128,129-320,321-640,641+].
- Add monitor: slab_frag>0.45 OR OOMs>0 in 15m -> auto-reduce batch caps and alert eng-ml-oncall.
- Schedule quant sweep (int4 vs int8-hybrid) focused on long-form tasks; liaison: hao + tara.

hao: I'll run the sweep over 48h and post a matrix (rouge/bertscore, p95/p99, tokens/cost).

tara: Filed tickets ML-9801 (defaults), ML-9802 (batcher bucketing), ML-9803 (quant sweep). Added short SOP on-call: if fragmentation spike -> set max_batch_size=1, max_new_tokens_default=128, enable compaction immediately and escalate if OOMs persist.

ben: Quick note: consider exposing a per-route "long-form" toggle in Console that routes to fp16 variant instead of int4 when enabled; we'll draft UX + warning text.

perf-bot: Staging stable for 45m. No OOMs.

(End)
